verdict.rationale: SavvyCal documents a public REST API that uses JSON and supports OAuth 2.0 and personal access tokens. Its documented endpoints cover the core scheduling actions: listing, creating and cancelling events, updating and duplicating links, and fetching available slots. That is enough for an agent to drive the product programmatically. missing for 10: a machine-readable OpenAPI spec (all probed paths returned 404) and an llms.txt (404), plus independent or hands-on corroboration of the API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The SavvyCal API adheres to REST conventions. Our API communicates in JSON format and uses OAuth access tokens to authenticate requests.
We offer several ways to integrate with our product, including a REST API, webhooks, and a JavaScript embed library.
Personal access token authentication ... Bearer format: pt_secret_XXXXXXXXX
List events GET /v1/events ... Cancel event POST /v1/events/{event_id}/cancel ... Create event POST /v1/links/{link_id}/events
